profile.campus: Aurora, Kane/DuPage County, Illinois (CyrusOne CHI3 building)
profile.reading:
Per two independent aggregator listings (datacentermap, datacenterHawk) agreeing on the address, corroborated by CyrusOne's own Aurora campus page, CHI3 sits at 2725 Bilter Road, Aurora, IL, part of the shared 450,000 sq ft / 114MW CHI1-CHI3 campus, distinct from the CHI1/CHI2 buildings on nearby Diehl Road.

CyrusOne acquired the original Aurora CME Group data center (now CHI1) in March 2016 for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to run its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease; CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.
profile.capacity_note: 114 MW total IT capacity published for the Aurora, Illinois (CHI1-CHI3) campus as a whole, not confirmed as this specific buildings individual figure, so not applied to the critical_it_mw column
profile.facility_note: CyrusOne CHI3, Aurora, Illinois, part of the CHI1-CHI3 campus on Bilter Road.
profile.research_note: Gap-view review: CHI3 is part of the CHI1-CHI3 campus whose only published figure is a 450,000 sqft / 114MW total shared across 3 buildings; no per-building breakout exists. No it_capacity_mw written.

reading.body:
CHI3 is one building in a three-building Aurora campus spanning 450,000 square feet with 114 MW of published IT capacity shared across all three buildings. The campus sits on Bilter Road in Kane and DuPage counties, acquired by CyrusOne from CME Group in 2016 and retained under private ownership by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners since 2022. No per-building capacity figure is published, so CHI3's individual IT load cannot be separated from CHI1 and CHI2.

If the 114 MW IT capacity were distributed evenly across the three buildings, CHI3 would represent roughly 38 MW, equivalent at 40 kW per rack to approximately 950 racks, a standard high-density AI training cluster. The full 114 MW campus at that density would support roughly 2,850 racks. Illinois has published 236 MW of colocation capacity across six mapped facilities, making this Aurora campus the seventh-largest by announced capacity in the state, though only 44 total facilities are mapped here.

The campus hosts CME Group's Globex matching engine under a 15-year lease from the 2016 acquisition, qualifying it to run mission-critical financial infrastructure. Beyond that anchor tenant, the campus specifications do not identify other current tenants or restrict its use to specific workloads. CyrusOne's portfolio has continued expanding under private ownership, with no published slowdown in capital deployment since the 2022 take-private transaction.
